CSK's Mahendra Singh Dhoni plays a shot against RCB ahead of Tata IPL match between Chennai Super Kings vs Royal Challengers Bengaluru at M.A.Chidambaram Stadium, Chepauk in Chennai. | Photo Credit: B. Jothi Ramalingam
F ranchises have reshaped their squads through four confirmed trades. Hardik Pandya moves from Mumbai Indians to Punjab Kings, with Arshdeep Singh heading the other way. Rishabh Pant returns to Delhi Capitals from Lucknow Super Giants, with Kuldeep Yadav moving to Lucknow.
Read more: Dhoni ends IPL playing career as CSK appoints him team mentor
On the deadline day for the IPL 2027 retentions, Mahendra Singh Dhoni retired from the league and, with it, brought the curtain down on his career as an active player. Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad have completed a four-player exchange.
Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards join Chennai, while Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis move to Hyderabad. Delhi and Hyderabad have also swapped T. Natarajan and Zeeshan Ansari.
The focus now shifts to final retention decisions and releases, before the mini-auction on December 16, 2026, in Goa.
The IPL paid tribute to Mahendra Singh Dhoni, thanking him for making the league “mighty special” and saying it looks forward to welcoming “Mentor MSD” soon.
Harshal Patel has been traded to Gujarat Titans from Sunrisers Hyderabad at a revised fee of ₹4 crore, the IPL announced.
Rajasthan Royals (RR) have signed India pacer Mohammed Shami and left-arm spinner M. Siddharth from Lucknow Super Giants (LSG), ahead of IPL 2027. Shami, acquired by LSG for ₹10 crore, moves at a revised fee of ₹8 crore, and Siddharth at his existing ₹75 lakh.
In a separate trade, England all-rounder Sam Curran moves from RR to LSG at his existing fee of ₹2.4 crore.
Hardik Pandya has left the Mumbai Indians. The all-rounder, a two-time T20 World Cup winner, has ended his second stint with the franchise in a direct swap with Punjab Kings’ Arshdeep Singh. His exit followed a difficult three years as captain, in which he appeared to lose favour with teammates and the franchise’s demanding fanbase.
Two-time Indian Premier League Purple Cap winner Harshal Patel is set to join Gujarat Titans from Sunrisers Hyderabad in an all-cash trade ahead of the retention deadline on November 17.
The Hindu understands that the 35-year-old pacer, whose expertise in the death overs has made him a sought-after commodity in the IPL, will move to the Ahmedabad-based franchise for ₹4 crore — half the price SRH paid to acquire him at the IPL 2025 auction.
Explosive Australia and Sunrisers Hyderabad opener Travis Head has decided to skip Indian Premier League 2027 to manage his workload ahead of a busy international schedule, according to a report.
Head has informed his franchise about his decision to opt out of the upcoming season and SRH are expected to release him, according to Cricinfo.
It is a day that fans of Chennai Super Kings and the wider cricket-watching public had been dreading. On the deadline day for the IPL 2027 retentions, Mahendra Singh Dhoni retired from the league and, with it, brought the curtain down on his career as an active player.
